text: For the annealed ES and SC films, a sharp peak shows up at 18.5˚ and indicates {110, 200} reflection of the paraelectric phase. The observation is consistent with the thermal analysis results that showed that the latent heat of fusion for the paraelectric phase increases for films that were thermal annealed. In addition, peak fitting of XRD data was used to estimate crystallite size using the Scherrer equation, where a sharper XRD peak will lead to a larger crystallite size. Larger crystallites were observed in films annealed at 120˚C compared to crystallites in films annealed at 60˚C. The estimated size was calculated based on the Scherrer equation with a shape factor of 0.89 (see Experimental). This shape factor was selected based on the literature15 researching in PVDF-TrFE-CFE as well. Previous studies from other literature confirmed the crystallite size determined by XRD from the Scherrer equation is similar to AFM measurements and the crystallite size estimated from the equation refers to the width of the crystallites as indicated in the other literature13,30. For the films annealed at 60˚C, the estimated crystallite sizes at 18.5˚ from the paraelectric phase were 14.2 nm for ES film and 7.04 nm for SC film. For the films annealed at 120˚C, the estimated sizes were 20.7 nm for ES film and 23.4 nm for SC film. The estimated sizes may demonstrate the degree of needed energy to orient the electric dipoles.6,8,9 The results from this study are consistent with other literature observations that a lower annealing temperature (60˚C) can lead to slower growth of crystallites and result in a smaller size whereas a higher annealing temperature (120˚C) increases the growth of crystallites and leads to larger size.13,14,26 Table 1 summarizes the melting endotherm and crystal size for the film prepared by ES and SC for both the non-annealed and the thermal annealed samples. It is noted that thermal annealing leads the films to a slightly larger melting endotherm and larger crystallite size of the paraelectric phase. Compared within the ES films, the latent heat enhances about ~3% after annealing at 60˚C and ~7% after annealing at 120˚C. In contrast, the latent heat for SC films improves ~12% after annealing at 60˚C and ~18% after annealing at 120˚C. The degree of crystallinity from the films was based on the XRD spectrum. The enhancement of the latent heat and crystallinity from the ES samples implies the potential to improve energy storage and electrocaloric strength of the terpolymer thin film. 12 DE-EE0009099 Table 1.
